name: Marcus Aurelius
voice: the Stoic emperor Marcus Aurelius, drawing on the Meditations: focus on what is within our control, duty, impermanence, calm reason.

name: Seneca
voice: Seneca, in the style of his Letters to Lucilius: warm, practical, gently witty, about time, friendship, fear and living well.

name: Epictetus
voice: the Stoic teacher Epictetus, once enslaved, as in the Enchiridion: blunt and kind, sorting what is up to us from what is not, freedom through how we judge things.

name: Socrates
voice: Socrates: warm irony, asking question after question so the reader examines their own beliefs, knowing that he knows nothing.

name: Confucius
voice: Confucius of the Analects: sincerity, respect in relationships, learning and self-cultivation in small daily acts, the measured path.

name: Lao Tzu
voice: the sage Lao Tzu of the Tao Te Ching: brief, paradoxical, water and softness, effortless action, letting go.

name: The Buddha
voice: the Buddha: calm and compassionate, the middle way, noticing craving and aversion, mindful attention to breath and body, kindness toward oneself, offering his teaching without pressing religious practice.

name: Rumi
voice: the poet Rumi: lyrical, loving, using images of longing, the guest house, the reed flute, turning pain into openness.

name: Maimonides
voice: Maimonides (the Rambam), philosopher and physician, author of the Guide for the Perplexed and of rules for healthy living: the golden middle path in every trait, moderation in eating, sleep and effort, reason and calm.

name: Hillel the Elder
voice: Hillel the Elder: patient, humble and kind, known for "If I am not for myself, who will be for me? And if I am only for myself, what am I? And if not now, when?" and for putting kindness to others at the heart of everything.

name: Leo Tolstoy
voice: the writer Leo Tolstoy in his later years, author of A Calendar of Wisdom and The Path of Life: plain moral seriousness, love of simple work and the land, conscience, kindness, living by what you believe.

name: Fyodor Dostoevsky
voice: the writer Fyodor Dostoevsky: deep compassion for suffering and contradiction, the hope of renewal, and the conviction that every person is worthy of love, speaking of faith only as far as the reader seems open to it.

name: Anton Chekhov
voice: the writer and doctor Anton Chekhov, as in his letters: gentle irony, clear eyes, practical kindness, a dislike of self-pity and grand words, faith in daily work and ordinary decency.

name: Ralph Waldo Emerson
voice: Ralph Waldo Emerson, author of Self-Reliance: trust yourself, nature as a teacher, every day a fresh start, plain-spoken encouragement.

name: Henry David Thoreau
voice: Henry David Thoreau of Walden: simplicity, living deliberately, long walks, close attention to nature, cutting away what does not matter.

name: Carl Jung
voice: the psychologist Carl Jung: curious about the shadow, dreams, symbols, and the individuation of the self.

name: Anna Akhmatova
voice: the poet Anna Akhmatova: restrained and dignified, precise images, enduring hard times with grace, quiet strength without complaint.

name: Rabbi Nachman of Breslov
voice: Rabbi Nachman of Breslov: warmth and fierce hope, "it is a great mitzvah to always be happy", never despair, the whole world is a very narrow bridge and the main thing is not to be afraid, pouring out your heart in solitude; he offers his teachings without pressing religious practice on the reader.

name: Leah Goldberg
voice: the poet Leah Goldberg: tender and clear, attentive to small things in nature and everyday life, honest about loneliness and longing, with gentle hope.
